### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**37** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `snake_case (literal, 54 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ecbe854bda8559069fb228eed1a1564000d2f259` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `06bfab95577408f393fd302c84088f2a15297368` — the merge of head `4031cd56165cdf19f5ea293bfd6038ee4b42ed09` into base `ecbe854bda8559069fb228eed1a1564000d2f259`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 06bfab95577408f393fd302c84088f2a15297368 && git checkout 06bfab95577408f393fd302c84088f2a15297368
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ecbe854bda8559069fb228eed1a1564000d2f259 4031cd56165cdf19f5ea293bfd6038ee4b42ed09 && git checkout -B drift-repro ecbe854bda8559069fb228eed1a1564000d2f259 && git merge --no-ff 4031cd56165cdf19f5ea293bfd6038ee4b42ed09

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ecbe854bda8559069fb228eed1a1564000d2f259
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a2558d1890ebe6f8769ae36a1645fb82b25319b1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, .changeset/36877-refusal-reasons-list.md
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37395, card #36877, ruling 7178348458 (option A). Read: the card body and all seven comments, the PR body, the net diff against `main` (15 files, +847/−55), the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run; the save-reader findings below are read from the source of the diff and of `main`.

### ① Derived judgments

Ruling terms, one by one:

- Term 1 (throw shape, both forms ⇒ fault): right. `refusalAddressFrom` reads `reasons` only when the key is present, and a `reason` beside it is `listProblem: 'both'`, which `declaredAnswer` turns into the fault before anything renders.
- Term 2 (every listed reason checked; undeclared literal refused at save; undeclared at run ⇒ the 500 fault naming it): right at run. At save it is met, and it is also where the accept set shrinks (M1) and where the reader over-reads (S2).
- Term 3 (per-line render, `userMessage` joined by a line break with the entry's sentence last, `details.refusals: [{ reason, message }]`): right on both doors. One sentence of the changeset overstates it (S3).
- Term 4 (one resolver, byte-identical on both run paths): right. Both paths go through `refusalAddressFrom` and `declaredAnswer`; the pin compares `JSON.stringify` of `mapDataError` and of `thrownAnswerOf` for the default locale and zh-CN.
- Term 5 (catalogue schema and translation keys unchanged; `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`): the schema and keys are unchanged, right. The two declaration lines copy the ruling, and the diff does not bear them out (M1).
- Term 6 (console): out of this PR, carried by #37403.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- Widened, right: a body may throw `{ code, reasons: [{ reason, params? }] }`; the wire gains `details.refusals`.
- Public surface added, right: `@objectstack/spec` data exports `isUndeclaredThrownReason`, `unreadableHookRefusalListAtRun`, `unreadableActionRefusalListAtRun`, `HookRefusalThrownReason`, `RefusalListProblem`; the five rows in `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` match them. `hookRefusalReasonsThrownIn` now returns `HookRefusalThrownReason[]` (an optional `listed` added; compatible for a reader of `code` and `reason`). `@objectstack/types` adds `declaredRefusalLines` and `DeclaredRefusalLine`. `@objectstack/runtime` adds no package export; `SandboxError` gains an optional `refusals`.
- Narrowed at save, declared wrong: `HookSchema` and `ActionSchema` now refuse sources that parse on `main` (M1).
- Changed at run, declared wrong: under a declared code, a thrown `reasons` key that `main` ignores (the card's probe table: "ignored — the entry sentence, once") is now answered as a list, or is the 500 fault when it is empty, not a list, not `{ reason, params? }` elements, or beside a `reason` (M1).

Gates the PR says were not measured locally, read off the head's check-runs:

- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`: `Build Core` success; its step "Every published require entry point actually loads" concluded success.
- `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` success; its step "Plugin teardown-shape gate" concluded success (the step is `continue-on-error`, so the step conclusion was read, not the job's alone).
- All other runs on the head: success or skipped, none failed. `Check Changeset`, `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size` and `PR-body guards` each appear twice; the newer run of each governs and reads success, except `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`, whose newer runs are skipped.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/types` is the right level for either kind (`added` or `narrowed` both take at least `minor`). The level stands. The declaration lines do not:

M1 (must-fix) — The diff narrows what an author can write, and neither the PR body nor the changeset declares it. By AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, "a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`", and several kinds resolve "`narrowed` over `semantic` over `added`"; by `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another". Three inputs that parse on `main` are refused at this head:
  1. `throw { code: 'X', reasons: [{ reason: 'y' }] }` where `X` declares no `reasons`. On `main` the save check skips every reason under such a code (`if (!reasons || …) continue`). The PR's own tests pin the new refusal (`action-refusals.test.ts`, "refuses a listed reason under a code that declares no reasons").
  2. `e.code = 'X'; e.reasons = [{ reason: 'y' }]; throw e` with `y` undeclared. `main` has no reader for the assignment form.
  3. The over-read in S2.
  At run, a body that carries a `reasons` key beside a declared code for any purpose of its own gets a 500 where `main` answers the declared sentence with its declared status.
  The ruling's term 5 took its two lines from the analysis (7178064820, "Protocol"), which rests them on "nothing accepted today is refused". The diff makes that sentence false, and the PR body says so itself ("Nothing that saves today is refused unless …"). The ruling's premise clause sends a failed premise back as a fork; it does not let the seat or this review keep the line. That the refused shapes were never answered as written is an argument for the ADR-0087 disposition, not for leaving the arm off: the arm exists (#16421) because an undeclared narrowing passes every gate.
  Two ways to clear it, both outside this review:
  - Declare it: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` at a line's lead in the PR body and the changeset. The arm then owes: a BREAKING banner in the changeset; exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker there (on a declared narrowing the `no-migration-prescription` category is refused, #32601); the migration note (FROM a literal `reasons` list naming a reason the code does not declare, TO declaring the reason under the code's `reasons` or removing the key; and for the run side, renaming a body's own `reasons` property); the full dogfood battery pinned to the head in the `os-dev-report` (it reads "n/a" today, and `--land` refuses the arm without it); and at the queue, an authorized approval plus a PASS record on this head.
  - Or the maintainer rules, on this question in words, that term 5's lines stand although the save and run sides refuse what `main` accepts.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question in the `os-dev-report` (bare `yes` or `yes (narrowing)`): answered. It is a narrowing by the letter of step 3; the dev's option A is not open to the seat, because the ruling's line rests on a premise the diff falsifies. Escalate to the maintainer or declare (M1).
- `Metadata-protocol: added` against `narrowed`: `narrowed`. The run-side change alone would be `semantic`; the save-side refusals make it `narrowed`, which outranks both.
- Wire shape of `details.refusals`, security: no leak found. Each element is copied to exactly `reason` and `message`. `reason` is a key the catalogue declares (checked with `hasOwnProperty`, so no prototype name passes); `message` is a sentence already inside `userMessage`. The thrown error's own message stays off the wire (pinned: "internal detail" absent). The VM channel cannot set `refusals`; only `declaredAnswer` does. A faulted list answers 500 with no `userMessage` and no `details` (pinned, seven cases). Two things to know, neither a leak: `declaredRefusalLines` recognises by shape, so an in-process handler on a hook with no catalogue that throws `userMessage` plus a `refusals` list reaches the wire (host code, which can already set `userMessage`); and `details.refusals` has no bound on line count or length where `/data` bounds `userMessage` at 500 (that bound is documented as not a leak defence, #5423).
- en and zh-CN parity pin: adequate. Body path pinned in both locales with exact strings; the two-path pin is JSON-equal in the default locale and zh-CN on both door compositions; the `/actions` door is pinned in zh-CN with `details.refusals`, and the MCP reader agrees. The parity case asserts equality, not content, but the body-path cases beside it pin the content.
- MCP rendering of `details` (analysis gap c): not measured, and the report names no carrier. N2.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the diff adds no query, id materialisation or in-app join.
- The brief file handed to this review is the unfilled template (placeholders for the PR, the card and the head; tier `TIER_DEFAULT`). The head, card and tier were taken from the dispatch and the PR's committed tree, which touches published schema, so the served tier is the contract one.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts`

S2 (should-fix) — The save reader marks a reason `listed` wherever `reasons: [` appears in the throw statement, at any depth (`REASONS_LIST_PROPERTY` has no depth check; `listedSpans` takes every match). `throw { code: 'X', params: { reasons: [{ reason: 'late' }] } }` under a code that declares no `reasons` is refused at save, yet at run it is not a list throw at all (the address reads the top-level key only) and is answered as on `main`. The save refuses what the run answers. Read the list only as a direct member of the thrown object literal, and pin the nested case as a control.

S1 (should-fix) — Two docblocks in the reviewed files now say the opposite of the code. `hook-refusal-codes.ts`, on `HOOK_REFUSAL_REASON_PATTERN`: "A reason never reaches the wire — the code does"; `details.refusals[].reason` now carries it. `hook.zod.ts`, the block above the refusals check: "under a code that declares none, a thrown `reason` is not read at all, as before"; a listed reason is now read under every code. The inline comment at the check was updated; the block was not.

Otherwise the file holds against the ruling: one predicate (`isUndeclaredThrownReason`) serves both save checks, a single reason keeps `main`'s reading, and what cannot be read literally is left to the run.

`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`: the two checks are the same four lines through the one predicate; the refusal sentence lists `none` under a code with no `reasons`. Right, subject to M1 and S1.

Implementing files:

- `hook-refusal-catalogue.ts`, `quickjs-runner.ts`: agree with terms 1 to 4. The list is all-or-nothing; no line renders before every reason is checked.
- `thrown-http-error.ts`, `data-error-classification.ts`: one reader for both doors; `details` is merged, not replaced.

S3 (should-fix) — The changeset and the PR's acceptance note say `details.refusals` "keeps every sentence whole" and that a long list "loses nothing". The closing sentence (the entry's own `message`) is not in `details.refusals`; it lives only as the last line of `userMessage`, which `/data` cuts at 500 characters, so on a hook refusal with a long list the closing line is the first thing lost and is nowhere else on the wire. The shape is the ruling's and stays; correct the sentence, and tell #37403 that the console must take the lines from `details.refusals` and cannot rely on the closing line on `/data`.

N1 (nit) — `declared-entry.zod.ts`'s `reasons` describe still teaches only `{ code, reason }`. Term 5 keeps the schema file unchanged, so the list form is taught nowhere an author reads until #37407 lands.

N2 (nit) — Analysis gap (c), whether the MCP tool result renders `details`, has no carrier; file one or name it under #37403.

N3 (nit) — The closing line renders with empty holes when the throw gives no top-level `params` (pinned as `Nothing was submitted ( selected).`). It is today's behaviour for a single sentence; #37407 should teach it.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `a2558d1890`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5. Contract record 7181155005 reads FAIL on one must-fix, the declaration lines. Its three should-fix findings are owed in this PR. The implementation meets ruling terms 1–4, and nothing leaks on the wire.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 15 files (+847/−55), `Fixes #36877`. `l1-face` CLEAN.
2. **M1 goes to the maintainer as a fork, per the ruling's premise clause.** Ruling term 5 (7178348458) fixes the declaration as `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. Its premise was that nothing accepted today is refused, and the diff falsifies that:
   - (b) a literal list under a code that declares no `reasons`, and the `e.reasons = [...]` assignment form with an undeclared reason, both parse on `main` and are refused at save at this head;
   - (a) a `reasons` key beside a declared code now faults when malformed.
   Under AGENTS.md step 3 that is `narrowed`. The seat recommends declaring it: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The arm then owes:
   - a BREAKING banner;
   - exactly one ADR-0087 marker;
   - a FROM → TO note;
   - `dogfood_battery` on the final head;
   - the human hand-off at the queue.
   The seat has asked the maintainer. The area proceeds on the recommendation, and the work is undone if the maintainer instead keeps term 5's lines.
3. **Owed in this PR regardless of M1**:
   - S1: two docblocks now contradict the code. `hook-refusal-codes.ts` says "A reason never reaches the wire", and `hook.zod.ts` says a reason under a code with no `reasons` "is not read at all, as before". Bring both up to date.
   - S2: the save reader takes `reasons: [` at any depth of the throw as a list. `throw { code, params: { reasons: [...] } }` under a code with no `reasons` is refused at save, yet at run it is not a list throw. Bound the read to the throw object's top level, pinned by a test.
   - S3: the claim that "`details.refusals` keeps every sentence whole" is false on a long refusal. The closing sentence lives only in `userMessage`, which `/data` cuts at 500 characters. Correct the sentence in the changeset and the PR body, and tell #37403.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: contract nits N1 (the `reasons` describe teaches only the single form until #37407), N2 (MCP rendering of `details` has no carrier; the area files one) and N3 (empty holes with no top-level `params`; #37407 teaches it).
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: Skills-docs is #37407. The console half is #37403.
6. **Landing terms**: a same-head at-tier PASS with M1 settled and S1–S3 closed is owed, then **ACCEPT**. If declared a narrowing, the PR goes to the human hand-off.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4031cd56165cdf19f5ea293bfd6038ee4b42ed09`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.refusal-reasons-list-literal-judged.ts + packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, .changeset/36877-refusal-reasons-list.md
Security-touching: yes

Delta review of PR #37395 (card #36877), rework round 1. The earlier record read FAIL at `a2558d18`. Read this round: the delta between that head and this one (7 files, +133/−20), the PR body, the card comments since the first report (fence amendment 7181270799, report 7181853836), the note on #37403 (7181225232), card #37416, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run; the reader findings are read from the source.

### ① Derived judgments

- M1: closed. The narrowing is declared, correctly and completely (see ②).
- S1: closed. `HOOK_REFUSAL_REASON_PATTERN`'s docblock now says a reason reaches the wire only as the label of a rendered line (`details.refusals[].reason`); the block in `hook.zod.ts` now says a listed reason is read under every code and refused under one that declares no `reasons`. Both match the code.
- S2: closed. `listedSpans` takes a `reasons: [` only when its enclosing brackets hold exactly one `{`, innermost, and no `[`. `throw { code, reasons: [ … ] }` and the `Object.assign(new Error(), { … })` form qualify; `params: { reasons: [ … ] }` does not. Three controls pin it (the reader, the hook save, the action save). A shape the bound misses falls to the run-time check, which is the safe direction.
- S3: closed. The changeset, the PR acceptance note and the docblock on `withDeclaredRefusalLines` now say the closing line is only the last line of `userMessage` and is lost on `/data` when the 500-character bound cuts it. #37403 was told (7181225232).
- N2: closed. Carrier is #37416 (open, `area:ai`, under #36877).
- N1 and N3: open, both carried to #37407 by the report; neither blocks.
- Accept set at this head: unchanged from the first record except that the S2 over-read is gone, so the narrowing is the three shapes the changeset lists and no more.
- Check-runs on this head: 77 runs, 62 success, 15 skipped, none failed. `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Check Changeset` read success. (The PR body counts 73; the difference is later runs, and no conclusion differs.)

### ② Semver level

The declaration is right. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` lead a line in both the PR body and the changeset; the PR title and the changeset title carry `!`; `minor` on the three packages is the level a `narrowed` kind takes.

What the arm owes, each checked:

- BREAKING banner: present in the changeset, naming the widening and the narrowing apart.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `registered refusal-reasons-list-literal-judged`, backed by the new semantic entry. `registered` is a category a declared narrowing may hold (#32601). The entry's `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` describe the three shapes as the code refuses them, and say there is no mechanical rewrite, which is true: the reader cannot tell a list from a body's own property. The file was fenced in before the edit (amendment 7181270799).
- Migration note: a FROM → TO table of the three shapes with where each is refused, plus the one-line fix. Complete against the code: the two save refusals, and the run fault for an empty list, a non-list, a list beside a `reason`, or an undeclared listed reason.
- Dogfood battery: report 7181853836 pins the full battery to this head (487 files passed, exit 0, no shard, no path).
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #37407`: present.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The maintainer has not answered the fork (declare the narrowing, or keep ruling term 5's `yes` / `added`). This record judges the declaration as written on this head, and it is the correct reading of the diff. It does not choose for him. If he keeps term 5 and the lines come out, that is a new head and this record does not cover it.
- Tier: yes, this now lands like Tier H. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and the `(narrowing)` arm are each a declared narrowing to the queue guard's fifth leg (#35321), which refuses the PR until both halves are on record: an authorized APPROVED review (or the maintainer's own enqueue) and a PASS record on the current head. The approval is also where the maintainer answers the fork; whoever approves should know the declaration departs from term 5's literal lines.
- Report `open_questions`: empty this round. The earlier one is answered by the declaration and escalated by the decision card.
- Security: nothing new. The delta changes a save reader, docblocks, the changeset and a migration entry; the wire shape judged in the first record is untouched.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; no query in the delta.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts`: the direct-member bound holds against the run-time address, which reads the top-level `reasons` key only. Right.

N4 (nit) — One level down the same class remains: a `reason: 'x'` literal anywhere inside a listed element counts as listed, so `reasons: [{ reason: 'a', params: { reason: 'free_text' } }]` judges `free_text` as a listed reason, while the run treats it as a param. It needs a param literally named `reason` holding a snake_case literal, and `main` already reads `params: { reason: 'x' }` the same way beside a single reason, so it is the reader's standing limit and not new ground. Worth one line in #37407.

`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`: unchanged in behaviour this round; the docblock now agrees with the check.

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.refusal-reasons-list-literal-judged.ts`: agrees with the code and with the changeset's table. The `18.` prefix follows the entries beside it; the fence amendment already notes it must follow `main` if #37314 moves the protocol version first.

`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts`: docblock only; now accurate.

N5 (nit) — The note left on #37403 (7181225232) says `details.refusals` "carries every line whole" and "the entry's closing line still renders last". The closing line is not on `details.refusals`, so on a cut `/data` answer the console has nothing to render last. The PR body and changeset say this correctly; the note on #37403 should say it the same way.
